title: Code2LoRA: Hypernetwork-Generated Adapters for Code Language Models under Software Evolution
summary: Code language models need repository-level context to resolve imports, APIs, and project conventions. Existing methods inject this knowledge as long inputs (retrieved through RAG or dependency analysis) or through per-repository fine-tuning and LoRA -- costly at repository scale and brittle to evolving codebases. We introduce Code2LoRA, a hypernetwork framework that generates repository-specific LoRA adapters, effectively injecting repository knowledge with zero inference-time token overhead. Co…
description: Code2LoRA, hypernetwork framework, LoRA adapters, repository-level context, parameter-efficient fine-tuning
developer_name: Liliana Hotsko, Yinxi Li, Yuntian Deng, Pengyu Nie

analysis.detail_brief: Code language models need repository-level context to resolve imports, APIs, and project conventions. Existing methods inject this knowledge as long inputs (retrieved through RAG or dependency analysis) or through per-repository fine-tuning and LoRA -- costly at repository scale and brittle to evolving codebases. We introduce Code2LoRA, a hypernetwork framework that generates repository-specific LoRA adapters, effectively injecting repository knowledge with zero inference-time token overhead.

title: Your UnEmbedding Matrix is Secretly a Feature Lens for Text Embeddings
summary: Large language models exhibit impressive zero-shot capabilities across a wide range of downstream tasks. However, they struggle to function as off-the-shelf embedding models, leading to suboptimal performance on massive text embedding benchmarks. In this paper, we identify a potential cause underlying this deficiency. Our motivation stems from an unexpected observation: text embeddings tend to align with frequent but uninformative tokens when projected onto the vocabulary space. We argue that th…
description: large language models, text embeddings, unembedding matrix, high-frequency tokens, dimensionality reduction
developer_name: Songhao Wu, Zhongxin Chen, Yuxuan Liu, Heng Cui, Cong Li et al. (6 authors)

analysis.detail_brief: Large language models exhibit impressive zero-shot capabilities across a wide range of downstream tasks. However, they struggle to function as off-the-shelf embedding models, leading to suboptimal performance on massive text embedding benchmarks. In this paper, we identify a potential cause underlying this deficiency. Our motivation stems from an unexpected observation: text embeddings tend to align with frequent but uninformative tokens when projected onto the vocabulary space.
